root_cause.text: The pruss_clk_mux_setup() function performs a double reference count decrement on clk_mux_np by calling of_node_put() both within the devm cleanup callback (pruss_of_free_clk_provider()) and again in the error path, because devm_add_action_or_reset() automatically invokes the cleanup callback on failure.
root_cause.evidence: The patch shows that devm_add_action_or_reset() on error already calls pruss_of_free_clk_provider() which decrements the reference count via of_node_put(clk_mux_np). The original code then jumps to the "put_clk_mux_np:" label and calls of_node_put(clk_mux_np) a second time. The fix removes the goto and the duplicate of_node_put() call, returning directly from devm_add_action_or_reset() to avoid the double free.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix error handling to ensure cleanup code executes and return the actual error code instead of always returning success when devm_add_action_or_reset() fails.
intent_record.what: Removed the error handling goto statement and early return after devm_add_action_or_reset() failure. Changed the final return from 'return 0' to 'return ret', allowing the function to continue to the cleanup label regardless of devm_add_action_or_reset() success or failure.
intent_record.how: Previously, if devm_add_action_or_reset() failed, the code would log an error and jump to put_clk_mux_np label. Now, the function logs the error but continues execution, falling through to put_clk_mux_np unconditionally via the return statement. This ensures the cleanup code (of_node_put) always executes and the actual error code is returned to the caller instead of always returning 0 on success.

relevance_review.reason: This group directly addresses the vulnerability root cause by fixing the error handling in devm_add_action_or_reset(). The fix ensures that when devm_add_action_or_reset() fails, the proper error code is returned instead of success, which prevents the double reference count decrement issue. By correctly handling the failure case, the cleanup callback won't be registered, avoiding the scenario where of_node_put() is called twice on clk_mux_np.

When devm_add_action_or_reset() fails, it automatically invokes the cleanup callback (pruss_of_free_clk_provider()) which calls of_node_put(clk_mux_np). The subsequent goto to put_clk_mux_np then calls of_node_put() again on the same reference, causing a double decrement of the reference count.

bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit ba59c9b43c86b2c2396acac94e41d946cbaec9fe
Author: Grzegorz Jaszczyk <grzegorz.jaszczyk@linaro.org>
Date:   Fri Sep 11 21:47:10 2020 -0700

    soc: ti: pruss: support CORECLK_MUX and IEPCLK_MUX
    
    The IEPCLK_MUX is present on all SoCs whereas the CORECLK_MUX is present
    only on AM65x SoCs and J721E. Add support for both these CLK muxes.
    
    This allows the clock rates and clock parents for these to be controlled
    through DT leveraging the clk infrastructure for configuring
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability exists in the pruss_clk_mux_setup() function. The function calls devm_add_action_or_reset(dev, pruss_of_free_clk_provider, clk_mux_np) at line 97-99, which registers pruss_of_free_clk_provider() as a cleanup callback. This callback (lines 23-27) calls of_node_put(clk_mux_np). However, if devm_add_action_or_reset() fails, the function still executes the error path at line 101 which calls of_node_put(clk_mux_np) again at line 101. Additionally, if any error occurs before the devm_add_action_or_reset() call succeeds (lines 47, 54, 61, 68, 75, 82, 89), the error path at line 101 calls of_node_put(clk_mux_np). The problem is that when devm_add_action_or_reset() succeeds and later an error occurs after that point, the cleanup callback will be invoked automatically by the devm infrastructure, and then the error path will call of_node_put() again, resulting in a double decrement of the reference count. The fix is not present - the code does not prevent the double put by either: (1) not calling of_node_put() in the error path after successful devm_add_action_or_reset(), or (2) removing the of_node_put() from the cleanup callback.
